title: Methodologies Explain Potential Differences in UCR Data
methodology_role: authoritative explanation of why publication tables diverge from explorer/master/open-data surfaces
v2_good_for: lane selection; reconciliation triage; deciding whether a mismatch is methodological instead of substantive
methodology_notes: Publication releases pass internal quality review and may exclude data; CDE/master-style surfaces keep all reported data in file.

title: UCR Summary of Reported Crimes in the Nation, 2024
methodology_role: defines the annual release structure and clarifies that CIUS contains reported, estimated, and trended data
v2_good_for: current annual-release semantics; coverage and cutoff framing; CIUS interpretation
v2_not_for: component-level machine ingestion when the underlying CIUS/NIBRS tables are available
methodology_notes: RCN 2024 is the umbrella release; CIUS is one component within it and mixes reported, estimated, and trended outputs.

title: Reported Crimes in the Nation, 2024 Frequently Asked Questions
methodology_role: documents annual cutoff dates, continued SRS acceptance, CIUS contents, and the absence of agency-level reporting-status details in the release
v2_good_for: explaining 2024 publication mechanics and why CIUS tables cannot answer agency reporting-status questions directly
methodology_notes: The FAQ states that tables 1-7 use traditional estimation for agencies lacking a complete 12 months and that agency reporting status must be checked in CDE rather than in RCN.

title: Crime Explorer Pages
unit_of_analysis: trend counts; rates; percentages; clearances; NIBRS demographic/characteristic views
methodology_role: dynamic monitoring surface with mixed data families
v2_good_for: current monitoring; quick context; anomaly triage; recent trend inspection
v2_not_for: stable annual controls; publication replication; point-in-time reproducibility unless externally frozen
methodology_notes: Violent/property views combine SRS data with summarized NIBRS data; remaining offenses are NIBRS-only; values can move as the dynamic surface refreshes.

title: Data Discovery Tool
unit_of_analysis: query-based crime counts plus agency lookup
methodology_role: interactive query and agency-discovery surface
v2_good_for: ORI lookup; agency-name reconciliation; quick offense queries; explaining CIUS table inclusions/exclusions
v2_not_for: publication control totals; raw incident extraction
methodology_notes: Violent/property queries explicitly apply the hierarchy rule, so the tool is not a drop-in substitute for raw NIBRS offense counting.

title: Agency Roster by State Abbreviation Endpoint
years: current roster; packet anchor pulled in 2024 workflow
unit_of_analysis: agency roster and current reporting-status fields
methodology_role: authoritative public roster and reporting-status surface
v2_good_for: ORI roster validation; agency type; county grouping; current is_nibrs; nibrs_start_date
v2_not_for: crime totals; blind year-specific source policy without effective-date logic
methodology_notes: Raw is_nibrs is current-status metadata; year-specific audits must derive effective status from nibrs_start_date.

title: Crime in the United States Annual Reports
geography_level: national; state; MSA; county; city; university; agency
methodology_role: official FBI publication-table lane for CIUS within the annual RCN release
v2_good_for: published FBI estimates; agency tables 8-11; static annual controls; release-consistent tables
v2_not_for: raw universe counts; current-month monitoring; agency reporting-status audits
methodology_notes: Tables 1-7 are traditional CIUS estimates; tables 8-11 are reported agency counts limited to agencies with 12 months of complete offense data.

title: Crime Incident-Based Data by State
methodology_role: raw NIBRS detail surface
v2_good_for: incident detail; ORI-level NIBRS support; offense/victim/property reconciliation
v2_not_for: FBI publication-style cross-era totals; direct comparison to hierarchy-rule or CIUS estimate tables without translation
methodology_notes: These are open-data style NIBRS records by state and year; they preserve detail that publication tables collapse or estimate away.

title: NIBRS Estimation Tables
geography_level: national; state; city-size and related table geographies
methodology_role: FBI-hosted NIBRS-only estimate table surface
v2_good_for: static FBI-hosted NIBRS estimate tables when V2 wants a download-package surface rather than API pulls
v2_not_for: raw reported counts; agency-level reconciliation; legacy SRS-estimate continuity
methodology_notes: CDE states these tables use methodologies developed in collaboration with BJS, so they belong to the NIBRS-estimate lane, not the CIUS publication lane.

title: Master File Downloads (Annual)
methodology_role: historical raw continuity and bulk extraction surface
v2_good_for: bulk engineering inputs; cross-year raw continuity; pre-CDE style master-file workflows
methodology_notes: Annual master files are fixed-length ASCII archives requiring programming knowledge; by methodology they retain all reported data in file.

title: Master File Downloads (Year-to-Date)
methodology_role: provisional in-year monitoring surface
v2_good_for: in-year monitoring before annual close
methodology_notes: Year-to-date files are provisional by design and should not anchor a stable V2 annual source lane.

title: Summary Reporting System (SRS) Estimated Crimes Dataset
methodology_role: traditional FBI estimate series
v2_good_for: long-run national/state continuity in the traditional FBI estimate lane
v2_not_for: NIBRS-only estimation; agency-level reconciliation; incident detail
methodology_notes: The download-page description says these state/national estimates were derived from SRS and match the estimates traditionally included in FBI annual publications.

title: Uniform Crime Reporting Program Participation Data
methodology_role: coverage-context surface
v2_good_for: state-year reporting coverage; denominator context; transition coverage framing
v2_not_for: crime totals; ORI roster authority; agency reporting-regime decisions
methodology_notes: The FBI describes this dataset as agencies reporting in any format and says it clarifies the percentage of population covered by reported data.

title: UCR Publications
methodology_role: pre-CDE publication-continuity surface
v2_good_for: pre-2020 publication continuity; archived methodology language and table definitions
methodology_notes: Use this for historical publication comparability; current annual releases moved to CDE/RCN packaging.

title: National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS)
methodology_role: BJS documentation hub for NIBRS and linked estimate products
v2_good_for: coverage framing; manuals and ICPSR references; locating official estimate products
methodology_notes: Useful for program context, not for V2 numeric controls.

title: Crime Known to Law Enforcement, 2024
methodology_role: human-readable benchmark publication for BJS/FBI NIBRS estimates
v2_good_for: official national/state estimate benchmarks; reliability and suppression context
methodology_notes: CKLE states that NIBRS estimates use imputation and weighting, and that prior-year values may be updated as late data are incorporated.

title: National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) National Estimates API
methodology_role: machine-usable national NIBRS-estimate surface
v2_good_for: machine pulls of current or archived national BJS estimates
methodology_notes: The API provides current revised endpoints and separate archive endpoints for originally published prior-year estimates.

title: NIBRS Estimation and Extract File Creation Methodology Report
methodology_role: current technical documentation for BJS estimate/extract creation
v2_good_for: audit trail for estimation and extract creation procedures
methodology_notes: The report describes how BJS receives FBI data, performs data quality checks, and constructs annual estimate/extract products.

title: Law Enforcement Agency Reported Crime Analysis Tool (LEARCAT)
geography_level: full-reporter states; counties; MSAs; selected large agencies
methodology_role: secondary exploratory NIBRS-reported-data surface
v2_good_for: exploratory reported-crime patterns in full-reporter states and large agencies
v2_not_for: official CDE/CIUS count matching; national annual controls
methodology_notes: LEARCAT is useful when its coverage rules fit the question, but it is not definition-identical to CDE and should not be used as a primary reconciliation authority.

title: LEARCAT Methodology
methodology_role: coverage and definition guardrails for LEARCAT
v2_good_for: explaining why LEARCAT counts/rates differ from CDE
methodology_notes: LEARCAT defines full-reporter states as 90%+ covered population and warns that some offense categories are defined differently than in CDE.

title: NIBRS Estimates Codebook and Supplementary Documentation
methodology_role: field interpretation for BJS estimate products
v2_good_for: interpreting estimate-domain fields, suppression flags, uncertainty fields, and geography variables
methodology_notes: Necessary when ingesting BJS estimate datasets programmatically.

title: Uniform Crime Reporting Program Data Series
methodology_role: secondary archival taxonomy only
v2_good_for: archival context on long-run UCR components
methodology_notes: Useful only as a taxonomy aid when situating legacy UCR collections; not an official V2 input surface.
